newsitem.title: USA: Florida church leader's wife charged with arson.
newsitem.headline: Florida church leader's wife charged with arson.

text.p: The wife of a prominent black church leader with ties to President Clinton has been charged with setting fire to a home he owned with another woman, the Pinellas County Sheriff's Department said Tuesday.

The department's spokeswoman said Deborah Lyons, the wife of Rev. Henry Lyons, was arrested shortly after the Sunday fire and charged with burglary and arson at a $700,000 house in a St. Petersburg suburb owned by her husband and Bernice Edwards.
Henry Lyons is president of the National Baptist Convention USA. The group has 8.5 million members, and is the largest black church group in the country.
Clinton spoke to the group at their annual meeting in New Orleans in 1994 and again in 1996 at a meeting in Orlando. He met with Lyons last year after a racial disturbance in St. Petersburg.
The sheriff's department said the fire caused damage to the house estimated at $30,000.
Deborah Lyons told the St. Petersburg Times the fire was started by accident after she had gone to the house to collect some papers for her husband, who was travelling in Africa.
She said the house was used as a guest home for visitors who came to speak to the church group and denied that her husband and Edwards were having an affair. She said they were business partners.
The department said the investigation was continuing and that Deborah Lyons had been released on bail.
